level_definitions.0: Absent, unsupported, or no verifiable evidence found under the frozen retrieval budget.
level_definitions.1: Minimal, experimental, obsolete, unusually narrow, or supported only by weak/single-path evidence.
level_definitions.2: Usable and verifiable but incomplete, uneven, limited in breadth, or materially constrained.
level_definitions.3: Mature and broadly usable with current evidence; meaningful capability exists with only moderate gaps.
level_definitions.4: Comprehensive, first-class or broadly established for the criterion with strong current verifiable evidence.

scoring.metric_score_formula: sum(level_points[component_level]) across the five fixed components; range 0..100

evidence_policy.snapshot_basis: The run's frozen created_at_utc date; every language shard in the run uses the same date.
source_priority: credible independent survey or technical source
community source only as supplementary evidence
evidence_policy.symmetry_rule: Use the metric selection_rule, the same five components, the same level definitions, and the same maximum retrieval depth for every language.
evidence_policy.not_executed_rule: Failure to obtain applicable evidence under the frozen retrieval budget is scored through the rubric; it is not N/A unless the metric is genuinely inapplicable under the benchmark's global N/A policy.
evidence_policy.popularity_rule: Raw package counts, stars, search-result counts or downloads may support one component but may not directly substitute for the metric score.

metric.third_party_library_availability_.selection_rule: Inspect the same five fixed domain groups for every language; prefer the official package index or official ecosystem directory, then independent package/project evidence.

components.criterion: Mature third-party libraries for web servers/clients, HTTP/networking and service development.
Mature third-party libraries for numerical, scientific, data-frame or data-processing workloads.
Mature third-party libraries for machine learning, AI or model-serving workloads.
Mature third-party libraries for databases, storage, serialization and common interchange formats.
Mature third-party libraries for application development concerns such as GUI/CLI plus testing/automation.

metric.package_ecosystem_activity_mainte.selection_rule: Use the primary package registry/ecosystem for the language when one exists and evaluate current observable maintenance within the fixed activity window; package count alone is never sufficient.

components.criterion: A usable package registry/index with search and metadata discovery.
Recent releases/updates across representative packages within the fixed activity window.
Version constraints, dependency metadata and compatibility information are routinely published.
Source and/or prebuilt package artifacts are routinely available through the ecosystem.
Security advisories, integrity/provenance metadata or comparable supply-chain mechanisms are available.

metric.third_party_tool_availability.selection_rule: Inspect the same fixed tool categories for every language and require independently maintained current tools; official first-party tools may be cited only as context, not as third-party availability.

components.criterion: Third-party IDE/editor integrations.
Third-party linting, formatting or static-analysis tools.
Third-party build, test or coverage tools.
Third-party debugging or profiling tools.
Third-party CI, release, packaging or developer-operations integrations.

metric.production_adoption_deployment_ev.selection_rule: Use public, independently checkable production evidence; named deployments must be documented by the deploying organization or corroborated by credible independent sources. Popularity surveys alone do not prove deployment.

components.criterion: Multiple named organizations have verifiable production deployments.
Evidence includes material scale, business-critical or infrastructure-critical workloads.
Deployments span multiple distinct industry/workload domains.
Evidence indicates current or recently maintained production use within the evidence window.
Evidence covers real deployed systems, not only prototypes, tutorials or developer preference surveys.

metric.community_public_knowledge_availa.selection_rule: Inspect the same knowledge channels for every language and use current, publicly accessible evidence rather than raw search-result counts alone.

components.criterion: Substantial searchable Q&A/discussion knowledge is available.
Independent tutorials, books, courses or long-form learning materials are available.
Conferences, meetups, user groups or comparable recurring community venues are active.
Public knowledge is being updated for current language/toolchain versions.
Knowledge is available across multiple regions/languages or otherwise shows broad community reach.

metric.core_tooling_availability_quality.selection_rule: Evaluate the maintained first-party/de-facto core developer toolchain actually available today; score implemented capability, not planned design.

components.criterion: Reliable compiler/interpreter/build-and-execute tooling.
Maintained formatter, linter or static-analysis support.
Maintained test-running support or standard test integration.
Documentation generation and/or package/project tooling integrated with the core workflow.
Core tools expose stable diagnostics, machine-readable output or comparable automation-friendly interfaces.

metric.package_dependency_management_qua.selection_rule: Evaluate the standard/de-facto package workflow using official documentation and current registry/tool behavior; ecosystem size is scored elsewhere.

components.criterion: Dependency resolution plus lockfile/reproducibility support.
Project manifests and expressive version/dependency constraints.
Workspace, multi-package or monorepo support.
Registry integrity, provenance, advisories or dependency-security mechanisms.
Documented package publishing, versioning and update workflow.

metric.ide_editor_support_quality.selection_rule: Inspect the same editor capabilities across at least the dominant general-purpose editor and any major dedicated IDE when available.

components.criterion: Syntax highlighting, navigation and symbol indexing.
Completion, signature help and type-aware analysis.
Refactoring and code-action support.
Integrated run/debug workflow.
Support exists across multiple relevant editors/IDEs and is actively maintained.

metric.debugger_profiler_support.selection_rule: Evaluate implemented, documented debugging/profiling workflows on current supported toolchains; generic OS tools count only when language-aware use is documented.

components.criterion: Breakpoints, stepping and variable/stack inspection.
Conditional breakpoints, watches, remote/core/post-mortem or equivalent advanced debugging.
Usable CPU/time profiling.
Usable memory/allocation/leak profiling.
Debugger/profiler workflows integrate with common IDEs/builds and cover multiple supported platforms.

metric.build_test_integration.selection_rule: Evaluate the standard/de-facto build-to-test-to-CI path with official tool documentation plus current integration evidence.

components.criterion: Standard or de-facto build tooling integrates with ordinary projects/packages.
Standard or mature de-facto test framework support.
Straightforward CI integration including version/platform matrices.
Coverage tooling and CI-gating/report support.
Build/test/coverage/lint configuration composes cleanly in project/workspace workflows.

metric.documentation_quality.selection_rule: Prioritize official current-version documentation, then independently maintained supplementary material; community size alone is not documentation quality.

components.criterion: Current official language reference/specification and tutorial material.
Current standard/core library API reference.
Task-oriented guides and representative examples.
Versioned docs, search/navigation and clear change/migration information.
Documentation-generation tooling and/or meaningful localization/community documentation support.

metric.installation_distribution_experie.selection_rule: Evaluate current official/de-facto installation paths on the same major desktop/server platforms and use only documented distribution channels.

components.criterion: Straightforward official or de-facto installation on Windows, macOS and Linux where applicable.
Package/version-manager installation paths reduce manual build requirements.
Multiple maintained distribution channels or prebuilt artifact routes.
Checksums, signing, provenance or comparable release-artifact integrity.
Clear current installation and upgrade documentation across supported platforms.

metric.toolchain_stability_release_matur.selection_rule: Score current observable release/support practices. Language age and first-release date are context only and never directly score.

components.criterion: Documented release cadence/process that is followed in practice.
Published supported-version/EOL or maintenance policy.
Documented compatibility/deprecation policy and controlled breaking-change process.
Reproducible/verifiable release artifacts, signing/provenance or comparable controls.
Stable documented governance/change-management process for toolchain evolution.

metric.implemented_platform_coverage.selection_rule: Count only platforms with currently implemented and documented build/run support; design intent without working support does not count.

components.criterion: Implemented support across Linux, macOS and Windows.
Implemented support across major CPU architectures such as x86-64 and ARM64.
Implemented mobile platform support where technically applicable.
Implemented embedded/bare-metal or constrained-device support where technically applicable.
Implemented WebAssembly/browser or other materially distinct deployment targets.

metric.external_integration_coverage.selection_rule: Evaluate working documented integrations and binding ecosystems, not only theoretical FFI design; FFI language design itself belongs to Language Quality.

components.criterion: Working C/native ABI or system-library integration ecosystem.
Maintained bindings/bridges to other major programming-language ecosystems.
Working database/data-system integrations.
Working network, cloud, container or service-platform integrations.
Practical embedding/extension/plugin mechanisms used by external systems.
